sheet-2-1.description: The main part of sheet 2, at 50 feet to an inch, is drawn with north to the left, so Washington Avenue runs across the sheet from left to right, south of the town centre. Church runs along the top edge, with dwellings, a car repair shop and supplies store and an iron store of the Empire Steel and Iron Co., the Presbyterian chapel and its parsonage; Furnace Brook flows under the block. Below Washington Avenue are dwellings, St. John's Dutch Reformed Church and, at the right, Academy rising to the top edge with the Miners' Union building, and Jonestown Road leaving Washington Avenue diagonally beside St. Rose R.C. Church and its rectory. The lower half of the part is the yard of the Empire Steel and Iron Co. blast furnace: many tracks and sidings, pig iron stock, the casting house, iron blast furnace and water jackets, laundry, electric motor, blacksmith, wheelwright, laborers' houses and brass moulding shop, slag dumps along the left edge and a long note on the furnace, which was closed and partly dismantled. A heavy line separates this part from the furnace stoves and air compressing plant at the lower right, which form part 2.
notes: North points to the left on this sheet.
Academy continues south of Washington Av as today's Mine Hill Road.
Placed from two junctions only (Washington Av at Jonestown Rd and at Academy): low confidence.

50 ft, north to the left. Part 1: Church, Washington Av, Jonestown Rd, Academy and the Empire Steel & Iron Co. blast furnace yard. Part 2 (lower right, behind heavy line): Empire Steel air compressing plant, no streets.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: Empire Steel & Iron Co. air compressing plant and blast furnace yard (lower right) (no street junction; railroad tracks only, none running today; needs step 6b, a feature carried from part 1).

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 covers the business centre of Oxford at 50 feet to an inch, drawn with north tilted about 16 degrees to the left. Washington Avenue runs down the sheet from its curved junction with Belvidere Avenue and Wall at the top to the bridge over Furnace Brook, where Kent Road branches off to the east and Washington Avenue continues south-east to the bottom edge. Buttzville Avenue leaves Wall northward at the top, with the Standard Silk Co. mill, its water tank and a fireproof building of 1913 in the block between Buttzville Avenue and County Road. Wall is lined on its south side by small stores, dwellings, the post office, lodge rooms, two garages and a dance hall. West of Washington Avenue are the M.E. Church, the old dismantled blast furnace, the public library and the arbitrary street Colden, with Lydia, also arbitrary, at the upper left. Furnace Brook crosses the sheet diagonally from the lower left to the upper right. Below Kent Road stand the Oxford Theatre, the Second Presbyterian Church and, on Church, the large Oxford Central High and Grammar Schools with a gymnasium. Stables of the Empire Steel and Iron Companies and a cinder dump fifty feet high occupy the lower left corner. Most of the sheet is frame dwellings and small commercial buildings; the large blocks east of Washington Avenue are largely open ground.
notes: Buttzville Av is now the north end of Washington Avenue; County Rd is Port Colden Road; Kent Rd is Washington Avenue (east-west stretch) and Kent Street; Colden roughly follows Cinder Street.
Lydia and Colden are marked arbitrary (names given by the map maker).
50 ft, single part: Washington Av, Belvidere Av, Wall, Buttzville Av, County Rd, Colden, Kent Rd, Church, Lydia; Standard Silk Co., Oxford Central School.

sheet-4-4.description: Part 4 of sheet 4 is the right-hand strip of the sheet, at 100 feet to an inch, showing the road north out of Oxford towards Buttzville. Buttzville Avenue runs down the middle of the part beside the D.L.&W. R.R., with Pequest Avenue branching off at the top. To the west, a lane and Upper Denmark Road enclose a block of small frame dwellings; east of the railroad, Old Buttzville Avenue and Lower Denmark Road run down the right edge with a few dwellings, a small store and outbuildings. A railroad water tank stands beside the tracks. The lower half of the part is open ground with one larger brick and frame house group near the bottom. The inset above the heavy line at the top right (part 3) shows Buttzville Avenue at the railroad station.
notes: Buttzville Av is today's NJ 31 and Pequest Av is Pequest Road; Upper and Lower Denmark Roads keep their names.
Anchored on the single junction of Buttzville Av and Pequest Av at the atlas scale with north from the drawn arrow: low confidence, especially at the bottom of the part.

Four parts. Part 1 (middle strip, 50 ft): Washington Rd (Mine Hill Road) and A St south of town. Part 2 (left strip, 50 ft): Buttzville Av with Road, Pequest Av, Lane. Part 3 (top right inset, 100 ft): Buttzville Av at D.L.&W. R.R. Part 4 (right, 100 ft): Upper Denmark Rd, Buttzville Av, Old Buttzville Av, Lower Denmark Rd.
Not georeferenced on this sheet: Washington Rd (Mine Hill Road) and A St south of town (50 ft) (no surviving junction (A St not in OpenStreetMap); needs parcel corners (step 6b)).

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Buttzville Av at the D.L.&W. R.R. station (100 ft) (no street junction; the railroad is abandoned; needs step 6b from part 4 or sheet 3).

sheet-5-1.description: The main part of sheet 5, at 100 feet to an inch, shows the eastern side of Oxford around the dye works and the hillside streets above Port Colden. The D.L.&W. R.R. crosses the upper part of the sheet with several tracks, a section house and curving sidings that run down the left side past the Oxford Foundry and Machine Co., makers of sash weights. Oxford Dye Works, Inc., cloth dyers, occupies a large group of brick buildings with an Empire Steel and Iron Co. general store, and the company's property extends over the blocks below. Front, Mechanic and Hill climb north-east from Port Colden in parallel, lined with small frame dwellings and the Lackawanna Hotel; Axford Avenue crosses the railroad and leaves the sheet at the top. Port Colden runs across the middle and continues east as Tunnel Hill, with vacant hillside beyond. To the south-west, Green Row, County Road, Bull Run and Academy fan out with rows of company dwellings, and Toulon, marked arbitrary, leads west to the foundry. A cow barn and barn yard sit at the top centre. The inset at the top left (part 2) and the area below the heavy line at the lower right (part 3) are separate parts.
notes: Front is today's Green Street, Mechanic is Axford Street, Port Colden and Tunnel Hill are NJ 31, Bull Run is Mechanic Street, Toulon roughly follows Port Colden Road.
Fit from three detected junctions and one hand-picked point with residuals of 3 to 12 m: low confidence.

100 ft. Part 1 (main): Front, Mechanic, Hill, Port Colden, Tunnel Hill, Axford Av, Toulon, Green Row, County Rd, Bull Run, Academy; Oxford Dye Works, Oxford Foundry. Part 2 (top left inset): Academy strip. Part 3 (lower right): Parks Av, Maple, Buckley Av, Lincoln Av, Henderson Av.
Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Academy strip (100 ft) (one street, no junction drawn; needs parcel corners along Academy Street (step 6b)).

sheet-5-3.description: Part 3 of sheet 5, at 100 feet to an inch, lies below the heavy line at the lower right of the sheet and shows the residential streets south-west of the town centre. Parks Avenue climbs from Buckley Avenue to Maple, which runs east along the top of a row of narrow lots; a narrow lane connects Maple back down to Buckley Avenue. Buckley Avenue crosses the bottom of the part from west to east with closely spaced frame dwellings on both sides, and a short cross street with two narrow lanes leads north from it into the blocks. At the right, Henderson Avenue runs down the edge of the part with Miller Street branching east, and Lincoln Avenue crosses at the top right corner. The rest of the part is large open lots, with woods and hillside beyond at the upper left and a block numbered 59 left mostly empty. Buildings are almost all small frame dwellings with stables and sheds.
notes: Parks Av is today's Maple Lane, Maple is Pine Street, Henderson Av is Henderson Street, Lincoln Av here is South Lincoln Avenue.
Placed from four hand-picked junctions; the detector paired lot lines on the narrow lanes. Low confidence.

100 ft. Part 1 (main): Front, Mechanic, Hill, Port Colden, Tunnel Hill, Axford Av, Toulon, Green Row, County Rd, Bull Run, Academy; Oxford Dye Works, Oxford Foundry. Part 2 (top left inset): Academy strip. Part 3 (lower right): Parks Av, Maple, Buckley Av, Lincoln Av, Henderson Av.
Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Academy strip (100 ft) (one street, no junction drawn; needs parcel corners along Academy Street (step 6b)).

sheet-6-1.description: The main part of sheet 6, at 100 feet to an inch, shows the western residential district along Belvidere Avenue, drawn with north turned about 37 degrees to the right. Belvidere Avenue enters at the upper left beside Old Belvidere Road, which runs parallel to it to the north-east and is linked back to it by B Street. Delta Place and Eden Place, both marked arbitrary, run north from Old Belvidere Road. At the centre Belvidere Avenue turns south at Mount Kisco Avenue, which runs east with pig yards along it, and continues down the sheet to the bottom edge. Henry runs parallel to it on the right, and School crosses between them; Candor Place and Clyde Place, both arbitrary, lead west from Belvidere Avenue. The blocks are filled with small frame dwellings and outbuildings; a vacant building and large open lots occupy the area west of Belvidere Avenue, and the eastern edge beside Henry is marked no exposure. The top strip along Belvidere Avenue (part 2) and the left strip along Jonestown Road (part 3) are separate parts divided off by heavy lines.
notes: Old Belvidere Rd and B St are today's Bush Street; Mt. Kisco Av is Mount Pisgah Avenue; School is the street mapped as Docker.
Placed from five hand-picked junctions with residuals of 6 to 13 m; the sheet appears drawn about 5 percent large. Low confidence.

100 ft. Part 1 (main): Belvidere Av, Old Belvidere Rd, B St, Delta Pl, Eden Pl, Mt Kisco Av, Henry, School, Candor Pl. Part 2 (top strip): Belvidere Av with Snyder. Part 3 (left): Jonestown Rd, Charlevoix St, Mine, Jones Rd, Soo Pl, Hillside Cemetery.

sheet-6-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 6 is the strip across the top of the sheet, at 100 feet to an inch, showing Belvidere Avenue west of the town as a straight road running from left to right with a row of frame dwellings, barns and sheds on both sides. Snyder leaves Belvidere Avenue southward near the left end of the strip and runs down to the heavy line that divides this strip from the main part of the sheet. House numbers run from about 597 at the left to 557 at the right. The lots behind the houses are deep and mostly open, with scattered outbuildings; a dashed no exposure line marks the left side. The sheet number 6 at the right edge shows that Belvidere Avenue continues onto the main part of the sheet.
notes: Snyder is today's Snyders Lane.
Anchored on the single junction with Snyder, at the atlas scale and the rotation of the drawn street lines: low confidence.

100 ft. Part 1 (main): Belvidere Av, Old Belvidere Rd, B St, Delta Pl, Eden Pl, Mt Kisco Av, Henry, School, Candor Pl. Part 2 (top strip): Belvidere Av with Snyder. Part 3 (left): Jonestown Rd, Charlevoix St, Mine, Jones Rd, Soo Pl, Hillside Cemetery.

sheet-6-3.description: Part 3 of sheet 6, at 100 feet to an inch, is the strip along the left side of the sheet showing Jonestown Road south-west of the town. Jonestown Road runs down the whole part, with a line of frame dwellings on its west side in the upper half. Hillside Cemetery lies along the left edge. A spur of the Empire Steel and Iron Co. railroad curves across the middle of the part, with Charlevoix Street, marked arbitrary, running parallel to it. In the lower half a small grid of company housing is laid out: Mine runs east from Jonestown Road, Soo Place, arbitrary, runs south from Mine, and Jones Road crosses the bottom of the part, with rows of small frame dwellings in blocks 75, 76 and 78. A heavy line separates the part from the main part of the sheet on the right.
notes: Mine is today's Renners Road, Soo Pl is 2nd Street, Jones Rd meets Jonestown Road where Jonestown Lane does today.
The north arrow on this part points straight up, but the fit puts north about 17 degrees to the left.
Placed from three junctions (one detected): low confidence.

100 ft. Part 1 (main): Belvidere Av, Old Belvidere Rd, B St, Delta Pl, Eden Pl, Mt Kisco Av, Henry, School, Candor Pl. Part 2 (top strip): Belvidere Av with Snyder. Part 3 (left): Jonestown Rd, Charlevoix St, Mine, Jones Rd, Soo Pl, Hillside Cemetery.

sheet-7-1.description: The main part of sheet 7, at 50 feet to an inch, shows the residential district around Belvidere Avenue and Lincoln Avenue west of the town centre, drawn with north turned about 53 degrees to the right. Winding Avenue, marked arbitrary, cuts across the upper left corner beside a small brook, and Zulauf Alley runs diagonally down to Belvidere Avenue. Belvidere Avenue runs down the sheet, with the Belvidere Avenue Hotel at its corner with Zulauf Alley. Henry runs parallel to it to the east, and Lincoln Avenue crosses the sheet from Henderson Avenue at the left edge to beyond Elm at the right. Miller, marked arbitrary, runs west from Belvidere Avenue to Henderson Avenue near the bottom. The blocks hold frame dwellings, stables, sheds and a bake oven; the area east of Henry is mostly open lots with chicken houses, and a garden truck farm lies beyond. A heavy line divides off the Replogle Steel Co. iron mine at the lower right (part 3), and an inset at the top right (part 2) shows Toulon and County Road at Furnace Brook.
notes: Henderson Av is today's Henderson Street, Miller is Scharrer Place, Zulauf Alley is Zulauf Lane, Henry is Henry Street, Elm is Elm Street; Lincoln Av west of Belvidere Av is South Lincoln Avenue.

50 ft. Part 1 (main): Winding Av, Zulauf Alley, Belvidere Av, Henry, Lincoln Av, Elm, Henderson Av, Miller. Part 2 (top right inset): Toulon, County Rd, Road at Furnace Brook. Part 3 (lower right): Replogle Steel Co. iron mine, no streets.
Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Toulon, County Rd and Road at Furnace Brook (garage and wagon shop) (no surviving junction identified; needs step 6b, carried from sheet 5 part 1 (Toulon)).
Not georeferenced on this sheet: Replogle Steel Co. iron mine (no streets; needs no evident control).
